What to Read After JLPT N5: A Practical Reading Path

Kanjidon Team · Jan 31, 2026

Finishing N5 study does not unlock one official shelf of books. The JLPT does not publish a fixed post-2010 kanji or vocabulary list, and “N5 level” labels from different publishers are not perfectly interchangeable. Choose your next reading by how much support you need and what you can understand—not by a promise that one title is universally next.

Use N5 as a Diagnostic, Not a Reading Ceiling

Official N5 material checks some basic Japanese through language knowledge, reading and listening. Real texts may use different vocabulary, formatting and cultural assumptions. A difficult first page does not mean you failed N5; it tells you which kind of support the text needs.

A Resource Ladder You Can Adjust

ResourceWhy it can helpHow to use it safely
Tadoku free booksGraded reading with several entry pointsStart where you can follow the story; move down if lookups dominate
Irodori materialsJapan Foundation lessons, audio and practical contextsChoose the part that matches your communication goal rather than a presumed JLPT equivalence
NHK News Web EasyCurrent short news written with learner supportExpect topic-specific vocabulary; sample one item before making it a daily target
Official JLPT samplesDirect evidence of the exam’s question styleUse for diagnosis, not as your only source of reading

Choose a Text by Friction

  • You can identify the topic without translating every sentence.
  • Unknown words do not prevent you from following every major event or claim.
  • The subject is interesting enough to reread after checking a few key items.
  • The format is usable: furigana, audio, glossary or short sections are available when you need them.
  • You can finish a meaningful unit before attention turns into guessing.

A Repeatable Reading Loop

  • Read once for the main idea and mark only the points that block it.
  • Look up the smallest set of words or grammar needed to restore the thread.
  • Reread the same section without the interruption.
  • Save a few useful words in their original sentence rather than copying every unknown item.
  • Return later or listen to the matching audio when the resource provides it.

When to Increase Difficulty

Move up when support feels optional rather than essential: you can follow the structure, infer some unfamiliar words and explain the text in simple terms. If comprehension collapses, step sideways to a different topic or shorter format. Reading growth is not a one-way staircase.

Sources and Reading Libraries

  • Official JLPT sample questions and practice workbooks
  • Official JLPT FAQ on fixed vocabulary and kanji lists
  • Tadoku free Japanese books
  • Japan Foundation Irodori learning materials
  • NHK News Web Easy
